content:
priya: quick async question — noticed some clients reporting that when they use stop=["\n", "\n###"] together with max_tokens the response sometimes includes the stop delimiter. expected behavior was deterministic truncation before the stop. seen on hosted and dedicated. anyone hit this?

jonathan: hmm, haven't seen that in the canary logs but i've seen oddness when requests hit the max_tokens boundary exactly. could be a race between streaming flush and stop detection.

maya: can you paste an example payload + model variant? might be quantization/streaming-specific.

priya: repro payload:```POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-3b-quant",
  "prompt": "Write a short policy summary:\n",
  "max_tokens": 64,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "top_p": 1.0,
  "stop": ["\n", "\n###"],
  "logprobs": 0
}
```response sometimes ends with "\n###" included (i.e. stop not stripped) and logprobs shows token with prob ~ -0.2 for the last token.

tomas: fwiw, our contract says stop sequences should trigger termination and be removed from returned text. that's been the API guarantee for years. if stop is present in final tokens we should strip it.

eva: tagging @jonathan for runtime/streaming. maya — can you check the decoder path when max_tokens == remaining_allowed? might be off-by-one.

jonathan: i'll repro locally. 2 quick notes: 1) with streaming we send partial chunks before final stop-check can run; 2) the post-processing strip happens in the handler that may run after stream end — if client closes early we might not strip.

maya: confirmed an off-by-one in the streaming boundary branch: when max_tokens is reached we call finalize_stream() which flushes buffer without re-running stop-filter on the buffered tail. simple fix: run stop-detection on final buffer before flush.

priya: nice find. do we need a migration/compat note? worried about backward compatibility if we change timing of strip (some clients rely on stop token still present? unlikely).

tomas: we should preserve contract: stop tokens must be removed. if any integration depended on presence that's a bug. put this behind a quick canary flag and roll to prod.

jonathan: plan: patch runtime to run stop-filter on finalize_stream (short PR), add a unit test for combinatorics of stop+max_tokens+streaming, add a canary rollout for 24hr. PR link when up.

maya: also spotted interplay with temperature/top_p ~= 0. when temp==0 & top_p==1 we see deterministic next-token that is the stop; with batching some sequences hit max_tokens then finalize_stream path. i will add a regression test with deterministic seeds.

priya: another related question — logprobs behaviour: if stop triggers termination should we include logprobs for the stop tokens in the response or not? current clients assume logprobs covers only returned tokens (i.e., post-strip).

jonathan: good call — contract: logprobs correspond to returned tokens. we should not leak logprobs for stripped tokens. tests should assert lengths match returned tokens.

eva: will you add a short blurb in the API docs under "generation semantics" explaining order: streaming chunks -> stop detection -> final strip -> logprobs align to returned tokens. make it explicit.

priya: yep i'll update docs + changelog. will also ping support and migration slack. can we also add an optional client-side flag to request raw stream (no post-strip) for debugging?

tomas: allowed behind admin/feature-flag only. but sounds useful for debugging.

ci-bot: build/22789 passed for branch fix/stream-stop-detection (unit tests + integration).

jonathan: cool — i'll open the PR now: https://git.redwood/internal/pulls/4521 — includes tests and canary config. please review when you have a minute.

maya: reviewing now, leaving inline comment on the finalize_stream call. small nit about log message verbosity. :thumbsup:

priya: thanks all. i'll schedule a short post-release sync tomorrow to confirm telemetry. if anyone needs me earlier ping DMs. :party:
